subject: Adaptive conditional routing
object: a superior safety paradigm for fully autonomous multi-agent AI systems operating in dynamic, unpredictable environments.
significance: This is the central thesis, establishing adaptive routing as the preferred architectural choice for safety in complex, unpredictable AI contexts.

subject: Rigidity (in AI system design)
object: a primary threat when confronted with unforeseen failures and 'unknown-unknowns'.
significance: This reframes rigidity from a perceived safety feature to a significant liability in dynamic environments, highlighting its inability to handle novel threats.

subject: Safety for autonomous AI in dynamic environments
significance: This defines a fundamental paradigm shift in AI safety architecture, moving away from static, pre-defined responses towards dynamic, adaptive capabilities.

subject: Robust, managed resilience
object: dynamic pathway adjustment, real-time component bypass, and conditional determinism.
significance: This details the core architectural mechanisms that enable the new safety paradigm, providing concrete examples of adaptive capabilities.

subject: Conditional determinism
object: provable guarantees for safety-critical functions within an otherwise adaptive system.
significance: This addresses a critical challenge of adaptive systems by showing how determinism can be selectively applied to ensure safety without sacrificing overall adaptability.

subject: 'Predictable failure' in safety-critical, autonomous AI
object: catastrophic mission failure or loss of life.
significance: This re-evaluates the concept of 'predictable failure,' arguing that in high-stakes AI, it is an unacceptable outcome rather than a desirable safety characteristic.

subject: The 'Oracle Problem' of exhaustive verification
object: any complex system in a truly dynamic environment, not just adaptive ones.
significance: This generalizes a key verification challenge, weakening the argument that adaptive systems are uniquely un-verifiable and placing the burden on all complex systems.
